# Careerden: product and public-site context

Careerden is a TypeScript open-source desktop job application tracker with a profile-aware CV creator and cover letter creator. It keeps opportunities, stages, salary and work-style context, interest, follow-ups, contacts, notes, match analysis, and application documents together from discovery through outcome. A user also maintains reusable profile details such as professional summary, skills, experience, education, projects, and certifications. In the current desktop workflow, a user submits a LinkedIn job-posting URL through a connected LinkedIn session and the application captures source and normalized job/company information. LinkedIn is the current automated capture source; direct manual application entry from other sources is planned and is not available in the current release. Depending on operator configuration and profile readiness, Careerden can run AI-supported requirement extraction and match analysis, then prepare editable CV and cover-letter drafts and rendered documents inside the tracked application.

## Intended workflow

1. A user creates and authenticates an account, then enters factual CV information in the Career
   Profile.
2. For custom document layouts, the user uploads CV and cover-letter DOCX templates. The public
   walkthrough presents this as the recommended setup; the product may also provide built-in layouts.
3. The user maps detected template variables to profile data and saves the mapping. Cover-letter
   content is mapped to the generated document-content field.
4. In the connected desktop app, the user submits a LinkedIn job-posting URL and may choose output
   language and tone. Careerden queues and processes the posting while preserving source material for
   traceability. Direct manual application entry from other sources is planned and is not available
   in the current release.
5. The captured opportunity becomes a trackable application record. The user can update its stage,
   interest, salary, work style, contacts, notes, and follow-ups while dashboard views show active
   applications, upcoming follow-ups, recent activity, and the application pipeline.
6. AI-supported analysis compares job requirements with the supplied profile and prepares editable
   CV and cover-letter content for the Application Pack.
7. The user reviews the overview, match evidence, CV, and cover letter; edits generated content when
   needed; and applies those edits with Update pack before deciding whether to use or submit the
   documents.

Careerden is not an automatic job-application service. It does not promise employment outcomes or guarantee the accuracy of AI output. Users should verify every generated statement.

The public marketing website explains the desktop product. It does not expose sign-in, signup, or
browser-application links. Its `/download` page detects the visitor's desktop operating system and
promotes the matching installer from the latest verified release, while also listing direct macOS
DMG, Windows EXE, and Linux AppImage downloads.

The public pricing section describes the current credit model. Every authenticated account receives
10 AI credits for each UTC calendar month. The $10 USD monthly subscription grants 100 credits for
each confirmed paid period, with applicable taxes potentially added at checkout. One completed
match analysis costs one credit; tracking remains available without credits. Unused credits expire
at the end of their applicable free month or paid period, and cancellation does not revoke credits
from a period already paid.

The public site links directly to the Careerden repository at
https://github.com/ErtanOzdemir/careerden. The repository is licensed under the GNU Affero General
Public License v3.0.

## Public workflow demonstration

The public landing page presents job-application tracking as the core workflow, followed by five
presentation-only setup and preparation steps: Add your profile, Upload your templates, Map the
variables, Add the application, and Review the pack and track progress. Its screen replicas use
fictional data and do not upload files, submit jobs, or persist onboarding progress. The public copy
does not claim a separate AI-regeneration action; it describes the current edit-and-Update-pack flow.

## Data categories described by the public policies

The intended workflow may process account and authentication data; professional profile information; job and company source/normalized data; application workflow events and preferences; match analysis; generated and uploaded documents; rendered files; support messages; reminders; security records; and essential technical/browser data.

Production controller details, lawful-basis mapping, subprocessor names, provider regions, international transfer mechanisms, retention periods, deletion timelines, security-control descriptions, analytics choices, contact details, company identity, complete billing and refund terms, governing law, and related business/legal details are not yet confirmed. The published draft pages mark these items explicitly for owner and legal review and do not claim GDPR certification or guaranteed compliance.

## Crawling guidance

Public product and policy pages may be indexed. `/onboarding` is a legacy noindex route that redirects
to the landing-page workflow. Authenticated application routes such as login, signup, applications,
profile, templates, settings, support, and API routes should not be indexed on any deployment that
shares a host.
